title: Why BIS testing is done
content: BIS states that testing in its laboratories is used to verify that manufacturers are capable of producing goods conforming to the relevant Indian Standards on a continuous basis. Testing supports grant of a licence, ongoing surveillance of licensees, and the Compulsory Registration Scheme.

title: BIS operates a network of eight laboratories
content: According to BIS, it has established a network of eight laboratories to support its conformity assessment schemes. Where BIS laboratories do not cover a particular test, testing is carried out in laboratories recognised or empanelled by BIS.

title: Finding which laboratory can test against a given Indian Standard
content: BIS states that full details of laboratories, their scope of testing and testing charges are available on the BIS LIMS portal (lims.bis.gov.in). The portal provides BIS lab-wise test facilities, recognised lab-wise test facilities, and an IS-wise view of which BIS, recognised or empanelled labs can test against a particular Indian Standard.

title: Product testing for CRS registration
content: Under the Compulsory Registration Scheme, a manufacturer must have the product tested by a BIS-recognised laboratory against the applicable Indian Standard. Registration is granted on the basis of that test report; unlike the ISI Mark scheme, CRS does not involve a BIS factory inspection.
